scope.summary: Cap recursive expression parsing in the std-only BUCK/Starlark syntax kernel so adversarially deep syntax fails closed before recursive parser exhaustion.
explicit_non_claims: No generated JSON face is edited.
No Cargo or workspace-level authority is changed.
No public parser API or caller-visible parse-budget parameter is introduced.
This does not claim full Starlark parsing, fuzzing, or deployed cloud-ci runtime evidence.

hyperscaler_capability_matrix.evidence: The existing parse(text) API remains stable; the safety limit is internal to the provider-neutral kernel.
AST nodes and byte spans remain unchanged; hostile depth returns ParseError instead of a partial model.
Parse, eval, edit, and guarded rewrite behavior stay in the same crate; targeted Buck2 build and unit tests pass.
The kernel has no filesystem, network, global state, or tenant data access; callers own tenant context.
The parser is a pure kernel. Authorization remains in cloud-ci/application callers.
MAX_EXPR_NESTING_DEPTH bounds recursive parser work for list, parenthesized, call, dict, and opaque-tail shapes.
No runtime service or tenant-billed operation is introduced.
This evidence file plus audit-chain row records the change; parser calls themselves remain pure and do not emit events.
ParseError carries an explicit nesting-depth message; runtime metrics are still owned by callers.
The kernel has no regional state or data residency surface.
Rollback is a normal signed git revert of a two-source-file parser change plus evidence.
Recursive parser denial-of-service input now fails closed under a deterministic depth cap.
Buck2 authoritative test/build evidence is captured in the PR verification and this multispectrum record.
No new caller config, dependency, or API migration is required.
No runbook is added; operational response is unchanged because callers already receive ParseError refusals.

facets.F1_correctness: The parser propagates depth through recursive expression entry points and returns ParseError once the limit is exceeded.
facets.F2_tests: The regression fixture builds nested list, parenthesized, call, dict, and opaque postfix-tail expressions and asserts an explicit nesting-depth refusal.
facets.F3_maintainability: A single parser-owned constant avoids a public parse-budget abstraction until callers demonstrate a real need.
facets.F4_compatibility: Existing AST structs, parse signature, and evaluation/edit exports are unchanged.
facets.F5_security: Adversarially deep BUCK syntax can no longer drive unbounded recursive parser descent.
facets.F6_privacy: No tenant, user, or personal data processing changes.
facets.F7_operability: Failure mode is a deterministic ParseError message rather than process exhaustion.
facets.F8_performance: Normal parse paths add one integer depth check per recursive expression; hostile deep inputs terminate early.
facets.F9_compliance: Rust + Buck2 remain authoritative; no cargo-test authority, no new dependency, and no generated face edit.
facets.F10_reversibility: Small signed commit can be reverted without data migration or generated-artifact regeneration.
facets.F11_observability: The explicit nesting-depth error can be surfaced by existing cloud-ci callers; no new telemetry adapter is introduced in the pure kernel.
facets.F13_migration: Strengthens the Rust-owned static-analysis substrate needed to retire shell/Python/CLI parser authority.

known_gaps: Remote oya-ci-required/cloud-ci context is pending until PR creation.
External reviewer approval and merge-queue admission remain pending.
The parser still relies on deterministic unit coverage rather than a fuzz corpus for all hostile syntax classes.
